import json
import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
from matplotlib.lines import Line2D

# Load data
with open('/app/benchmark/source_data.json', 'r') as f:
    data = json.load(f)

records = data['model_benchmarks']['data']
df = pd.DataFrame(records)

# Define dimensions order to highlight crossings
dimensions = [
    "Knowledge Recall",
    "Language Understanding",
    "Reasoning",
    "Inference Speed",
    "Instruction Following",
    "Code Generation",
    "Math / Quantitative",
    "Multimodal Understanding"
]

# Define colors
family_colors = {
    "GPT": "#1f77b4",     # tab:blue
    "Claude": "#9467bd",  # tab:purple
    "Gemini": "#2ca02c",  # tab:green
    "LLaMA": "#ff7f0e",   # tab:orange
    "Qwen": "#d62728"     # tab:red
}

# Distinguish top models
top_models = ["GPT-4o", "Claude 3.5 Sonnet", "Gemini 1.5 Pro", "LLaMA 3.1 405B", "Qwen2.5 72B"]

fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(16, 9))

# Plot vertical axes
for i, dim in enumerate(dimensions):
    ax.axvline(i, color='#333333', alpha=0.4, linewidth=1.5, zorder=1)

# Plot each model
for _, row in df.iterrows():
    y = [row[dim] for dim in dimensions]
    x = list(range(len(dimensions)))
    
    is_top = row['model'] in top_models
    lw = 4.0 if is_top else 1.5
    alpha = 0.9 if is_top else 0.4
    
    color = family_colors.get(row['family'], '#000000')
    
    # Plot line
    ax.plot(x, y, color=color, linewidth=lw, alpha=alpha, zorder=3 if is_top else 2)
    
    # Add markers
    ax.scatter(x, y, color=color, s=80 if is_top else 30, alpha=alpha, zorder=4 if is_top else 2)

    # Label top models on the right side
    if is_top:
        offset_y = y[-1]
        if row['model'] == 'GPT-4o':
            offset_y += 1.5
        elif row['model'] == 'Claude 3.5 Sonnet':
            offset_y -= 1.5
        
        ax.text(x[-1] + 0.1, offset_y, row['model'], ha='left', va='center', 
                fontsize=11, fontweight='bold', color=color, 
                bbox=dict(facecolor='white', alpha=0.6, edgecolor='none', pad=1))

# Axis styling
ax.set_xticks(range(len(dimensions)))
ax.set_xticklabels(dimensions, rotation=15, ha='right', fontsize=12, fontweight='bold', color='#222222')
ax.set_xlim(-0.5, len(dimensions) + 0.8)
ax.set_ylim(20, 105)
ax.set_ylabel("Normalized Score (0-100)", fontsize=13, fontweight='bold', labelpad=15)
ax.set_title("AI Model Capabilities: Trade-offs Across 8 Dimensions", fontsize=18, fontweight='bold', pad=30, color='#111111')

# Background styling for data-dense theme
ax.set_facecolor('#fafafa')
fig.patch.set_facecolor('#ffffff')
ax.grid(axis='y', color='#dddddd', linestyle='--', alpha=0.8)
for spine in ax.spines.values():
    spine.set_visible(False)

# Legend
legend_elements = [Line2D([0], [0], color=color, lw=4, label=family) for family, color in family_colors.items()]
legend_elements.append(Line2D([0], [0], color='#777777', lw=4.0, label='Flagship Models (Thick)'))
legend_elements.append(Line2D([0], [0], color='#777777', lw=1.5, alpha=0.5, label='Lightweight Models (Thin)'))

ax.legend(handles=legend_elements, loc='upper center', bbox_to_anchor=(0.5, -0.15), ncol=7, fontsize=12, frameon=False)

plt.tight_layout()
plt.savefig('/app/output/result.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
